title: Environmental Dynamic Mechanical Analysis to Predict the Softening Behavior of Neural Implants
protocol: Synthesize the softening thiol-ene polymer according to previous protocols inside a fume hood.
Prepare a 20 mL glass vial for polymer mixing.
Cover the vial in aluminum foil to prevent incident light from contacting the monomer solution.
Keep the vial at room temperature (RT).
Add 50 mol% of 1,3,5-triallyl-1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6(1H,3H,5H)-trione (TATATO) to the covered vial using a disposable plastic pipette.
Add 45 mol% of trimethylolpropane tris(3-mercaptopropionate) (TMTMP) to the vial.
Add 5 mol% of Tris[2-(3-mercaptopropionyloxy)ethyl] isocyanurate (TMICN) to the vial.
Add 0.1 wt% of the photoinitiatior 2,2-dimethoxy-2-phenylacetophenone (DMPA) to the polymer solution.
Mix the contents inside the vial thoroughly by planetary speed mixing without exposing the solution to light.
Spin coat the polymer solution as thin films between 5 to 50 µm in thickness on microscopic glass slides or silicon wafers according to the spin curve.
Transfer the polymer films on the carrier substrate immediately after spinning to the crosslinking chamber.
Photo-polymerize the films for 60 min under 365 nm UV bulbs.
Post-cure the films for 24 h in a vacuum oven at 120 °C.
Cut the cured polymer films into rectangular samples with widths of 4.5 mm and lengths of 50 mm for DMA testing.
Set the CO2 laser micromachining parameters to 5.0% power (2.0 W) and 10.0% speed (0.254 m/s).
Define the DMA samples using photolithography in a Class 10000 cleanroom facility.
Deposit low temperature silicon nitride as a hard mask for plasma etching processes.
Pattern the device outline/shape using standard lithography techniques.
Use a plasma etcher with SF6 and O2 plasma to remove the hard mask and SMP layer, respectively.
Etch the remaining silicon nitride hard mask away in diluted 10:1 HF dip.
Delaminate the test devices from the glass slide/wafer by soaking in deionized water as the last step.
Use a dynamic mechanical analyzer (DMA) with an immersion system equipped for tension mode.
Connect the liquid nitrogen to the machine and enable LN2/air as a gas source for the furnace.
Write the method for dry measurements using the machine software, including conditioning, oscillation temperature ramp, and conditioning end of test steps.
Set the mode for conditioning options to active and select “tension”.
Set axial force to 0.05 N with initial value on, sensitivity at 0.0 N, and proportional force mode in force tracking.
Compensate for modulus by selecting “on”, then set dynamic force to 25.0% with minimum axial force of 0.05 N.
Programmed extension below 0.0 Pa is enabled with strain adjust set to 0.05%, minimum strain at 0.1%, maximum strain at 0.5%, minimum force at 0.05 N, and maximum force at 0.2 N.
Set start temperature for oscillation temperature ramp to 10 °C with soak time off and wait for temperature on.
Ramp rate is set to 2.0 °C/min with end temperature at 100 °C, soak time after ramp off, sampling rate at 1 pts/s, strain % at 0.275%, single point mode, and frequency at 1 Hz.
Set the following parameters for the conditioning end of test: environmental control off.
Set the axial force adjustment on.
Disable mode.
Transducer/motor off.
Write the method for immersion testing with machine software including four steps: conditioning, oscillation-time, oscillation-temperature ramp, and conditioning-end of test.
Set the following parameters for the conditioning options: mode active.
Select “tension”.
Axial force 0.05 N.
Initial value on.
Sensitivity 0.0 N.
Proportional force mode force tracking.
Compensate for modulus on.
Select “axial force”, dynamic force to 25.0%.
Minimum axial force 0.05 N, programmed extension below 0.0 Pa.
Mode enabled, strain adjust 0.05%, minimum strain 0.1%, maximum strain 0.5%, minimum force 0.05 N, maximum force 0.2 N.
Set the following parameters for the oscillation time: temperature 39.5 °C.
Inherit set point off.
Soak time 0.0 s.
Wait for temperature off.
Duration 3600.0 s.
Sampling rate 1 pts/s.
Strain % 0.275%.
Single point, frequency 1 Hz.
Set the following parameters for the oscillation temperature ramp: start temperature 10 °C.
Inherit set point off.
Soak time 300.0 s.
Wait for temperature off.
Ramp rate 2.0 °C/min.
End temperature 85 °C.
Soak time after ramp 300.0 s.
Sampling rate 1 pts/s.
Strain % 0.275%.
Single point, frequency 1 Hz.
Set the following parameters for the conditioning end of test: environmental control = off, axial force adjustment = on, mode disabled, transducer/motor = off.
Measure the actual thickness of the polymer specimen for dry (in air) testing with Caliper with 0.001 mm precision.
Enter the sample name, description, and sample geometry into the software.
Set the loading gap to 15 mm and load the sample.
Center and align specimen before the clamps are screwed hand tight or use a torque wrench with 0.1 N.
Close the furnace and start the measurement using the methods described in section 2.2.
Wait until the measurement is over.
Open the furnace and remove the polymer sample from the machine.
Measure the actual thickness of the polymer specimen for immersion testing in PBS with Caliper with 0.001 mm precision.
Enter the sample name, description, and sample geometry into the software.
Prepare the setup with the immersion beaker fixed with a clamp at the upper grip.
Set the loading gap to 15 mm and load the sample.
Center and align the specimen before the clamps are screwed hand tight or use a torque wrench with 0.1 N.
Place the immersion bath on the bottom fixture and screw it tightly.
Fill the bath with RT PBS.
Place the lid on top.
Close the furnace.
Start the measurement immediately using the methods described in section 2.3.
Ensure that the drain is closed.
Wait until the measurement is over.
Remove the PBS from the immersion baths using the drain.
Open the furnace.
Remove the lid from the beaker.
Unscrew the immersion beaker.
Lift it and remove the polymer sample from the machine.
Clean the clamps and immersion beaker with de-ironed water to remove any remaining salt from the PBS.
Measure the polymer in air without the immersion beaker.
Follow the instructions for sample loading and unloading as described in section 3.
Repeat this measurement at least 3x to gather results with statistical relevance.
Measure the polymer inside the immersion bath following the steps described in section 4.
Repeat the measurement at least 3x to gather results with statistical relevance.
Open the results tab in the machine software, where the raw data can be viewed in a table format or plotted as a graph.
Plot the first part of the immersion measurement, the oscillation-time measurement, as storage modulus over time to evaluate the softening kinetics.
Note the time at which modulus levels out.
Repeat measurement with increased immersion time if polymer is not fully softened after 1 hour.
Display oscillation-temperature ramps of measurements in air and PBS as storage modulus on left axis and tan delta on right axis over temperature.
Plot dry (air) and PBS measurement data together to display changes due to plasticization.
Note the storage modulus of dry material at 25 °C.
Note the storage modulus of soaked sample at 37 °C.
Note the changes in tan delta peak between dry and soaked samples.
Export data as .txt or .csv file for further interpretation.
